title: Chemical spills into drainage ditch at SpaceXAI in Southaven

content_html:
MEMPHIS, Tenn. — Cleanup efforts are underway after thousands of gallons of a chemical spilled into a drainage ditch at the SpaceXAI facility in Southaven on Saturday, according to the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality.

SpaceXAI said that a misconfigured hose attached by a contractor to a mobile tank resulted in the release of approximately 5,000 gallons of propylene glycol.

“Much of the fluid remained contained on-site; however, some flowed into a nearby drainage ditch,” SpaceXAI said.

The company said that the team immediately stopped the flow to prevent further travel down the ditch and initiated cleanup.

Cleanup began within hours and is expected to be completed by the end of Sunday, SpaceXAI said.

“We are working directly with an adjacent landowner to ensure all impacted areas are appropriately addressed,” said SpaceXAI.

On Sunday, the MDEQ said the chemical involved has been identified as “DOWFROST HD Heat Transfer Fluid.”

According to Dow, the manufacturer, the product is classified as a nonhazardous mixture under OSHA standards.

“The material has been contained, and there is no immediate threat to public health or safety. MDEQ is overseeing removal efforts to ensure the material is properly managed and to protect surrounding water resources,” said the dept.

“Thorough cleanup includes removing all residual fluid from the affected area, and there is little concern for lasting environmental impacts due to its low toxicity and solubility in water,” said SpaceXAI.

The MDEQ said they monitored cleanup efforts after the spill at around 8:25 p.m. on Saturday.

Mid South Environmental Services, the cleanup contractor, will continue recovery operations and excavate and properly dispose of impacted soil along the silt fence, MDEQ said.

MDEQ said SpaceXAI will coordinate additional cleanup efforts and conduct periodic inspections to identify and remove any remaining material.

Saturday night, when WREG crews attempted to enter Stanton Road, which is a public road, SpaceXAI’s security team escorted our photographer off the property.
